requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue-unichar
requirements.canonical: The `decvalue_unichar` predefined function has the signature decvalue_unichar(inout universal charstring encoded_value, out any decoded_value, in charstring string_serialization := "UTF-8", in universal charstring decoding_info := "", in universal charstring dynamic_encoding := "") return integer.
requirements.original:
decvalue_unichar(inout universal charstring encoded_value,
             out any decoded_value, 
             in charstring string_serialization:= "UTF-8",
             in universal charstring decoding_info := "",
             in universal charstring dynamic_encoding := "") 
             return integer

requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue-unichar
requirements.canonical: The `decvalue_unichar` function IS the predefined function that decodes (part of) a universal charstring into a value.
requirements.original: The decvalue_unichar function decodes (part of) a universal charstring into a value.

requirements.subject: ent:test-system
requirements.canonical: The test system SHALL treat a prefix of the universal charstring `encoded_value` passed to `decvalue_unichar` as an encoded instance of the actual type of `decoded_value`.
requirements.original: The test system shall suppose that a prefix of the universal charstring encoded_value represents an encoded instance of the actual type of decoded_value.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue-unichar
requirements.canonical: The optional `decoding_info` parameter of `decvalue_unichar` IS used for passing additional decoding information to the codec.
requirements.original: The optional decoding_info parameter is used for passing additional decoding information to the codec and, if it is omitted, no additional information is sent to the codec.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue-unichar
requirements.canonical: If the `decoding_info` parameter of `decvalue_unichar` is omitted, no additional decoding information IS sent to the codec.
requirements.original: The optional decoding_info parameter is used for passing additional decoding information to the codec and, if it is omitted, no additional information is sent to the codec.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue-unichar
requirements.canonical: The optional `dynamic_encoding` parameter of `decvalue_unichar` IS used for dynamic selection of the encode attribute of the `decoded_value` parameter for this single `decvalue_unichar` call.
requirements.original: The optional dynamic_encoding parameter is used for dynamic selection of encode attribute of the decoded_value parameter for this single decvalue_unichar call.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue-unichar
requirements.canonical: The dynamic selection of the encode attribute in a call of `decvalue_unichar` IS governed by the rules of clause 27.9.
requirements.original: The rules for dynamic selection of the encode attribute are described in clause 27.9.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue-unichar
requirements.canonical: If decoding by `decvalue_unichar` is successful, the part of `encoded_value` consumed by decoding (the used characters) IS removed from the `encoded_value` parameter.
requirements.original: If the decoding was successful, then the characters used for decoding are removed from the parameter encoded_value, the rest is returned (in the parameter encoded_value), and the decoded value is returned in the parameter decoded_value.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue-unichar
requirements.canonical: If decoding by `decvalue_unichar` is successful, the remaining undecoded part of the input IS returned in the `encoded_value` parameter.
requirements.original: If the decoding was successful, then the characters used for decoding are removed from the parameter encoded_value, the rest is returned (in the parameter encoded_value), and the decoded value is returned in the parameter decoded_value.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue-unichar
requirements.canonical: If decoding by `decvalue_unichar` is successful, the decoded value IS returned in the `decoded_value` parameter.
requirements.original: If the decoding was successful, then the characters used for decoding are removed from the parameter encoded_value, the rest is returned (in the parameter encoded_value), and the decoded value is returned in the parameter decoded_value.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue-unichar
requirements.canonical: If decoding by `decvalue_unichar` is unsuccessful, the value of each of the actual parameters for `encoded_value` and `decoded_value` IS NOT changed.
requirements.original: If the decoding was unsuccessful, the actual parameters for encoded_value and decoded_value are not changed.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue-unichar
requirements.canonical: The `decvalue_unichar` function SHALL return an integer value indicating success or failure of the decoding.
requirements.original: The function shall return an integer value to indicate success or failure of the decoding below:

requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue-unichar
requirements.canonical: The return value 0 of `decvalue_unichar` IS the indication that decoding was successful.
requirements.original: The return value 0 indicates that decoding was successful.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue-unichar
requirements.canonical: The return value 1 of `decvalue_unichar` IS the indication of an unspecified cause of decoding failure.
requirements.original: The return value 1 indicates an unspecified cause of decoding failure.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue-unichar
requirements.canonical: If the `encoded_value` actual parameter of `decvalue_unichar` contains an uninitialized value, `decvalue_unichar` SHALL return 1.
requirements.original: This value is also returned if the encoded_value parameter contains an unitialized value.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue-unichar
requirements.canonical: The return value 2 of `decvalue_unichar` IS the indication that decoding could not be completed because `encoded_value` did not contain enough characters.
requirements.original: The return value 2 indicates that decoding could not be completed as encoded_value did not contain enough bits.

ambiguity.issue: `encoded_value` of `decvalue_unichar` is a universal charstring; the text (copied from decvalue) speaks of 'bits'. Canonical text uses 'characters'.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue-unichar
requirements.canonical: Each restriction of clause 16.1.2 IS applicable to `decvalue_unichar`.
requirements.original: The restrictions in clause 16.1.2 apply.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue-unichar
requirements.canonical: If the optional `string_serialization` parameter of `decvalue_unichar` is omitted, the default value "UTF-8" IS used.
requirements.original: If the optional string_serialization parameter is omitted, the default value "UTF-8" is used.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue-unichar
requirements.canonical: The `string_serialization` actual parameter of `decvalue_unichar` SHALL be one of "UTF-8", "UTF-16", "UTF-16LE", "UTF-16BE", "UTF-32", "UTF-32LE" or "UTF-32BE".
requirements.original: The following values (see ISO/IEC 10646 [2]) are allowed as string_serialization actual parameters (for the description of the UCS encoding scheme see clause 27.5): a) "UTF-8" b) "UTF-16" c) "UTF-16LE" d) "UTF-16BE" e) "UTF-32" f) "UTF-32LE" g) "UTF-32BE"

requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue-unichar
requirements.canonical: The octet serialization of the characters used by `decvalue_unichar` SHALL NOT include the optional signature (byte order mark).
requirements.original: The serialized bitstring shall not include the optional signature (see clause 10 of ISO/IEC 10646 [2], also known as byte order mark).

readings: The octet serialization of the characters used by `decvalue_unichar` SHALL NOT include the optional signature (byte order mark).
The `decvalue_unichar` function SHALL NOT produce or expect a byte order mark in the bitstring exchanged with the codec.
The universal charstring handled by `decvalue_unichar` SHALL NOT start with the character U+FEFF.
ambiguity.issue: 'The serialized bitstring' is not a parameter or result of `decvalue_unichar` (which handles a universal charstring); it is unclear which bit/octet sequence must be free of the BOM. The first reading (the intermediate octet serialization) was chosen.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue-unichar
requirements.canonical: When `string_serialization` of `decvalue_unichar` is "UTF-16" or "UTF-32", big-endian ordering SHALL be used.
requirements.original: In case of "UTF-16" and "UTF-32" big-endian ordering shall be used (as described in clauses 10.4 and 10.7 of ISO/IEC 10646 [2]).

requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue-unichar
requirements.canonical: A call of `decvalue_unichar` IS equivalent to converting `encoded_value` with oct2bit(unichar2oct(encoded_value, string_serialization)), calling `decvalue` on the result with `decoded_value`, `decoding_info` and `dynamic_encoding`, and returning the `decvalue` result.

ambiguity.issue: The explanatory function and its description name the parameter `string_encoding` (with a stray quote in the default "UTF-8""), while the signature in C.5.4-s001 names it `string_serialization`.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue-unichar
requirements.canonical: If the inner `decvalue` call of `decvalue_unichar` returns 0, `encoded_value` IS assigned oct2unichar(bit2oct(remaining bitstring), string_serialization).

ambiguity.issue: The explanatory function and its description name the parameter `string_encoding` (with a stray quote in the default "UTF-8""), while the signature in C.5.4-s001 names it `string_serialization`.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue-unichar
requirements.canonical: The `decvalue_unichar` function IS executed by first converting the universal charstring passed in `encoded_value` into an octetstring using `unichar2oct`.
requirements.original: The decvalue_unichar function first converts the universal charstring value passed in the encoded_value parameter into an octetstring using the unichar2oct function.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue-unichar
requirements.canonical: The `string_serialization` parameter of `decvalue_unichar` IS the control of how the characters are converted into octets (i.e. how the bitstring sent to the codec contains the characters).
requirements.original: The string_encoding parameter controls how the characters are converted into octets (in fact how the bitstring sent to the codec contains the characters).

ambiguity.issue: The explanatory function and its description name the parameter `string_encoding` (with a stray quote in the default "UTF-8""), while the signature in C.5.4-s001 names it `string_serialization`.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue-unichar
requirements.canonical: The octetstring produced inside `decvalue_unichar` IS converted into a bitstring by `oct2bit`.
requirements.original: The octetstring is subsequently converted into a bitstring by the oct2bit function.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue-unichar
requirements.canonical: The bitstring produced inside `decvalue_unichar` IS passed to the standard `decvalue` function, which performs the actual decoding.
requirements.original: This bitstring is then passed as a parameter to the standard decvalue function that performs the actual decoding.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue-unichar
requirements.canonical: If decoding by `decvalue_unichar` is successful, the undecoded part of the message IS converted from bitstring to octetstring by `bit2oct` and then to universal charstring by `oct2unichar`.
requirements.original: In case of successful decoding, the undecoded part of the message is automatically converted from bitstring to octetstring by the bit2oct function and then to universal charstring using the oct2unichar function.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue-unichar
requirements.canonical: If decoding by `decvalue_unichar` is successful, the universal charstring obtained from the undecoded part IS assigned to the `encoded_value` parameter.
requirements.original: This universal charstring is then assigned to the encoded_value parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-decvalue-unichar
requirements.canonical: The result of the inner `decvalue` call IS returned to the caller as the result of `decvalue_unichar`.
requirements.original: The result of decoding is then returned to the TE, finishing the decvalue_unichar call.

ambiguity.issue: 'TE' (TTCN-3 Executable, a TRI/TCI concept) is not defined in the core language; the result is returned to the calling behaviour.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-encvalue-o
requirements.canonical: The `encvalue_o` predefined function has the signature encvalue_o(in template (value) any inpar, in universal charstring encoding_info := "", in universal charstring dynamic_encoding := "", out integer bit_length) return octetstring.
requirements.original:
encvalue_o(in template (value) any inpar,
         in universal charstring encoding_info := "",
         in universal charstring dynamic_encoding := "",
         out integer bit_length) return octetstring

requirements.subject: ent:fn-encvalue-o
requirements.canonical: The `encvalue_o` function IS the predefined function that encodes a value or template into an octetstring.
requirements.original: The encvalue_o function encodes a value or template into an octetstring.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-encvalue-o
requirements.condition: the actual parameter passed to inpar is a template
requirements.canonical: When the actual parameter passed to the `inpar` formal parameter of `encvalue_o` is a template, the template SHALL resolve to a specific value.
requirements.original: When the actual parameter that is passed to inpar is a template, it shall resolve to a specific value (the same restrictions apply as for the argument of the send statement).

ambiguity.issue: The standard calls `send` an operation (clause 22.2.1); 'send statement' deviates from that term.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-encvalue-o
requirements.canonical: The actual parameter passed to the `inpar` formal parameter of `encvalue_o` IS subject to the same restrictions as the argument of the `send` operation.
requirements.original: When the actual parameter that is passed to inpar is a template, it shall resolve to a specific value (the same restrictions apply as for the argument of the send statement).

ambiguity.issue: The standard calls `send` an operation (clause 22.2.1); 'send statement' deviates from that term.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-encvalue-o
requirements.canonical: The octetstring returned by `encvalue_o` IS the encoded value of `inpar`.
requirements.original: The returned octetstring represents the encoded value of inpar, however, the TTCN-3 test system need not make any check on its correctness.

requirements.subject: ent:test-system
requirements.canonical: The test system NEED NOT check the correctness of the octetstring returned by `encvalue_o`.
requirements.original: The returned octetstring represents the encoded value of inpar, however, the TTCN-3 test system need not make any check on its correctness.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-encvalue-o
requirements.canonical: The optional `encoding_info` parameter of `encvalue_o` IS used for passing additional encoding information to the codec.
requirements.original: The optional encoding_info parameter is used for passing additional encoding information to the codec and, if it is omitted, no additional information is sent to the codec.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-encvalue-o
requirements.canonical: If the `encoding_info` parameter of `encvalue_o` is omitted, no additional encoding information IS sent to the codec.
requirements.original: The optional encoding_info parameter is used for passing additional encoding information to the codec and, if it is omitted, no additional information is sent to the codec.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-encvalue-o
requirements.canonical: The optional `dynamic_encoding` parameter of `encvalue_o` IS used for dynamic selection of the encode attribute of the `inpar` value for this single `encvalue_o` call.
requirements.original: The optional dynamic_encoding parameter is used for dynamic selection of encode attribute of the inpar value for this single encvalue_o call.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-encvalue-o
requirements.canonical: The dynamic selection of the encode attribute in a call of `encvalue_o` IS governed by the rules of clause 27.9.
requirements.original: The rules for dynamic selection of the encode attribute are described in clause 27.9.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-encvalue-o
requirements.canonical: Each general error cause of clause 16.1.2 IS applicable to a call of `encvalue_o`.
requirements.original: In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:

requirements.subject: ent:fn-encvalue-o
requirements.condition: no encoding function exists for the actual type of inpar
requirements.canonical: A call of `encvalue_o` SHALL cause an error when encoding fails due to a runtime system problem, i.e. when no encoding function exists for the actual type of `inpar`.
requirements.original: In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are: Encoding fails due to a runtime system problem (i.e. no encoding function exists for the actual type of inpar).

requirements.subject: ent:fn-encvalue-o
requirements.condition: the encoded message is not octet-based and its bit length is not divisible by 8
requirements.canonical: If the encoded message is not octet-based and its bit length is not divisible by 8, the encoded message IS left-aligned in the octetstring returned by `encvalue_o`.
requirements.original: In case the encoded message is not octet-based and has a bit length not divisible by 8, the encoded message will be left-aligned in the returned octetstring and the least significant (8 - (bit length mod 8)) bits in the least significant octet will be 0.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-encvalue-o
requirements.condition: the encoded message is not octet-based and its bit length is not divisible by 8
requirements.canonical: If the encoded message is not octet-based and its bit length is not divisible by 8, each of the least significant (8 - (bit length mod 8)) bits of the least significant octet returned by `encvalue_o` IS 0.
requirements.original: In case the encoded message is not octet-based and has a bit length not divisible by 8, the encoded message will be left-aligned in the returned octetstring and the least significant (8 - (bit length mod 8)) bits in the least significant octet will be 0.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-encvalue-o
requirements.canonical: The bit length of the encoded message CAN be assigned to a variable through the `out` formal parameter `bit_length` of `encvalue_o`.
requirements.original: The bit length can be assigned to a variable by usage of the formal out parameter bit_length.

readings: The `bit_length` out parameter of `encvalue_o` is mandatory and always receives the bit length of the encoded message.
The `bit_length` out parameter of `encvalue_o` is optional and may be skipped by the caller when the bit length is not needed.
ambiguity.issue: 'can be assigned' and the position of `bit_length` after defaulted parameters leave open whether the actual parameter may be omitted; out parameters have no default value, so the mandatory reading was chosen.

non_requirement.reason: Introduces the TTCN-3 function in C.5.4-s020; the semantics are extracted from that code unit.
